summary: A directory compiled by the Network Information Center of how to get accounts at various ARPANET sites, issued after many requests. For each site it lists an address, contacts and what kinds of accounts are available. Corrections were to be sent to the NIC for the next Resource Notebook.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC lists contacts and account information for ARPANET sites. It invites corrections for a later edition of the Resource Notebook.

subtitle: A directory of account information for ARPANET computer sites.

tldr.problem: Users had requested information about opening accounts at ARPANET sites.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists site addresses, contacts, and reported account arrangements, including experimental and paid use.
tldr.outcome: Readers are asked to send corrections to the NIC for inclusion in a later Resource Notebook.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 518's status as Unknown. This RFC is a dated directory of site account information.

sections.title: Finding an Account at a Network Site
sections.content:
RFC 518 responds to requests for information about opening accounts at ARPANET sites. For each listed site, it provides an address, contact information, and a description of account availability.

Readers are asked to send additions or changes to Jake Feinler at the NIC before July 15, 1973, for a next Resource Notebook.
sections.plainLanguage: The directory helps users find out whom to contact about accounts at network sites. The NIC asks readers to report corrections.

sections.title: Different Sites, Different Terms
sections.content:
The entries describe varied arrangements. Some sites offered experimental accounts; some sold computer time; some limited file storage or required individual requests. Other entries say information was not yet available.

The RFC gives contact details for each listed site rather than setting common account rules across the network.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site set its own terms. The directory reports whether experimental accounts or paid computer time were available and whom to contact.

sections.title: Keeping the Directory Current
sections.content: The RFC asks readers to send changes and additions to the NIC for a later Resource Notebook. This makes the notice a dated directory rather than a permanent account policy.
sections.plainLanguage: The listed details could change, so readers were asked to send updates to the NIC. The notice is a directory, not a shared account system.
